algorithms.name: bounding-box-calculation
algorithms.html: The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="bounding-box-calculation-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">bounding box calculation algorithm</dfn> consists of the following steps.

steps.html: With the model scene loaded and normalized to model space, set the animation to the first frame if present.
let max be a new DOMPoint with values of -Infinity.
let min be a new DOMPoint with values of Infinity.
let queue be an empty list of elements.
Add the model’s root object to queue.
While <var>queue</var> is not empty:
set element to the last element in queue and remove it from queue.
If element contains any child elements, add them to queue.
If element contains renderable geometry, find the minimum and maximum value for the X, Y and Z locations of that geometry.
Apply the world matrix of element to the bounding box of its geometry.
set each value of min to the minimum of its current value and the minimum for this element’s bounding box.
set each value of max to the maximum of its current value and the maximum for this element’s bounding box.
Set the values of boundingBoxCenter to be the mean of each values of min and max.
Set the values of boundingBoxExtents to be each value of min subtracted from max.

algorithms.name: model-fit
algorithms.html:
The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="model-fit-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">model fit algorithm</dfn> takes a <var>rotation</var> argument and consists of the
following steps.

steps.html: Let bounds be the resource’s stored bounds, previously calculated using the bounding box calculation algorithm.
Let extents be the extents of bounds.
Let center be the center of bounds.
Let width and height be the laid-out content-box dimensions in CSS pixels, each multiplied by 0.0254 / 96 to obtain CSS-derived meters in element space.
Let xScale be width divided by extents.x, or positive infinity if extents.x is zero.
Let yScale be height divided by extents.y, or positive infinity if extents.y is zero.
Let scale be the minimum of xScale and yScale. If both are positive infinity, set scale to 1. If either viewport dimension is zero, set scale to 0.
Set entityTransform to a uniform scale of scale and the supplied rotation.

Translate the model so that center, after applying the scale and rotation, is aligned with the center of the viewport in X and Y, and is scale × extents.z / 2 behind the viewport plane. The translation must account for the scaled and rotated position of center. With the identity rotation used for initial fitting, the front face of the scaled bounding box lies on the viewport plane and the rest lies behind it.

algorithms.name: automatic-fitting-after-resize
algorithms.html:
When either dimension of the loaded model element’s content box changes after layout,
the user agent MUST perform the following steps:

steps.html: If automatic fitting enabled is false, preserve entityTransform and return.
If the element is in orbit mode, apply the orbit fit algorithm, preserving the current rotation.
Otherwise, apply the model fit algorithm with the current rotation as its rotation argument.

algorithms.name: orbit-fit
algorithms.html: The <dfn class="dfn-paneled has-dfn-panel" data-dfn-type="dfn" data-noexport="" id="orbit-fit-algorithm" role="button" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">orbit fit algorithm</dfn> consists of the following steps.

steps.html: Let bounds be the resource’s stored bounds, previously calculated using the bounding box calculation algorithm.
Let extents be the extents of bounds.
Let center be the center of bounds.
Let diameter be the Euclidean length of extents: sqrt(extents.x² + extents.y² + extents.z²). This is the diameter of a sphere centered on center that encloses the bounding box.
Let width and height be the laid-out content-box dimensions in CSS pixels, each multiplied by 0.0254 / 96 to obtain CSS-derived meters in element space.
Let scale be the minimum of width and height, divided by diameter. If diameter is zero, set scale to 1. If either viewport dimension is zero, set scale to 0.
Preserve the model’s current rotation and replace the scale in entityTransform with a uniform scale of scale.

Translate the model so that center, after applying the scale and rotation, is aligned with the center of the viewport in X and Y, and is scale × diameter / 2 behind the viewport plane. The translation must account for the scaled and rotated position of center, so that the enclosing sphere lies entirely behind the viewport plane.
Apply subsequent orbit rotations about this fitted center, preserving its position. The enclosing sphere then remains within the viewport at any orientation.
